# The Stan Ecosystem

Stan is not one piece of software — it's an **ecosystem** of ~50 repositories that together take a user from "I have data and a scientific question" to "I have a fitted, checked, and validated Bayesian model."

Understanding the layers is the fastest way to know where you can contribute.

## Four layers

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
```
Layer 4 — Workflow & analysis
  posterior · bayesplot · loo · priorsense · rstanarm

Layer 3 — Language interfaces
  cmdstanr · cmdstanpy · rstan

Layer 2 — Command-line engine
  cmdstan

Layer 1 — Compiler & math
  stanc3 · stan · math
```
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="html" unless-format="revealjs"}
```
┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  LAYER 4 — Workflow & downstream analysis (mostly R packages)      │
│  posterior · bayesplot · loo · priorsense · projpred · shinystan   │
│  rstanarm · rstantools · posteriordb                               │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  LAYER 3 — User-facing interfaces (one per language)                │
│  cmdstanr · cmdstanpy · rstan · MatlabStan · Stan.jl …              │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  LAYER 2 — The command-line engine                                  │
│  cmdstan                                                             │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  LAYER 1 — The compiler & the math                                  │
│  stanc3 (Stan → C++ transpiler)  +  stan (algorithms & services)    │
│  math (C++ autodiff library — the actual computational engine)      │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
:::

## The pipeline

A Stan program is:

**`stanc3`** (transpile) → **`stan` + `math`** (compile & sample) → **`cmdstan`** or an interface → **`posterior` / `bayesplot` / `loo`** (analyze draws)

## Which repo should I touch?

| If you want to… | Start here |
|---|---|
| Add a distribution or fix autodiff | **math** |
| Add Stan language syntax | **stanc3** |
| Improve sampling algorithms | **stan** |
| Improve the CLI | **cmdstan** |
| Better R/Python UX | **cmdstanr** / **cmdstanpy** |
| New diagnostic or summary stat | **posterior** |
| New visualization | **bayesplot** |
| Better model comparison | **loo** |
| Fix docs or add a tutorial | **docs**, **example-models** |

## Entry points by background

| Your background | Good first repos |
|---|---|
| Statistics / applied Bayes | `bayesplot`, `loo`, `docs`, `example-models` |
| R programming | `cmdstanr`, `posterior`, `bayesplot`, `rstanarm` |
| Python programming | `cmdstanpy` |
| C++ / numerics | `math`, `stan` |
| Compilers / OCaml | `stanc3` |
| Technical writing | `docs`, `example-models` |

::: {.content-visible when-format="html" unless-format="revealjs"}
See [stan-ecosystem-guide.md](stan-ecosystem-guide.md) for the full repository catalogue, dependency graph, and Bayesian-workflow mapping.
:::

## Key takeaway

Pick a layer that matches your skills. Most workshop participants with an R background will find **Layer 3–4** the most accessible entry point.
